attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
EVENT MEDICAL PLAN
Women on the Move Community Run 7K, Sunday 11 July 2027
Applicant: Women on the Move Port Halden
Issue: 1.2

1. Event summary
A 7K race with 60 runners, starting at 08:00 in the Tanners Row area of Port Halden. We expect a crew from Lifeline Event Medics on the day, though we have nothing in writing yet.

2. First aid cover
3 first aid posts will operate, at the start, at the finish and at the course midpoint, staffed by 12 qualified first aiders. Posts are placed so that no part of the course is more than 1.5 km from one. Two cycle responders move along the course with defibrillators.

3. Weather and hydration
Water is available every 2.5 km. The race director checks the forecast 48 hours and 2 hours before the start. Above 28 degrees C the start is brought forward or the course shortened, and above 32 degrees C the race is cancelled. In cold or wet conditions, foil blankets and a warm shelter are at the finish.

4. Transfer to hospital
The receiving hospital is Harbourside Medical Centre, 3 km from the finish. The transfer route and the pick-up point at the top of Union Row have been walked with the first aid team. The hospital's emergency department has been told the date and the expected numbers.

5. Communications
Every first aid post and cycle responder carries a radio on the medical channel, with phones as backup. All calls for an ambulance go through the medical lead, who gives the crew the access point and the nearest barrier to open.

6. Clinical lead
The medical lead is Ines Moreau, a registered paramedic, who is on site from an hour before the start until the last runner is cleared. The lead can have any runner withdrawn on medical grounds.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
RACE PLAN
Women on the Move Community Run 7K | Sunday 11 July 2027
Organiser: Women on the Move Port Halden
Race director: Anita Bose
Reference: RQ-17066

Overview
The Women on the Move Community Run 7K is a 7K race of 7 km for 60 entrants, based in the Tanners Row area of Port Halden. The start is at 08:00 and the course closes at 09:30.

Course
The course runs in order along Union Row, Hatter Street, Bridge Row, Ash Avenue and Vine Street, all of which are closed to traffic for the race. Major roads crossed: Tram Street and Queen's Road. The finish is in the Civic Plaza.

Course dimensions
Most of the course follows the older street grid. Measured building line to building line, Union Row is about 5.5 m, Vine Street about 4 m, and parked vehicles on Bridge Row leave around 5 m. The field assembles on Union Row over that width, and the finish chute is laid out in the same street, ahead of the Civic Plaza.

Support
Entrants collect numbers from the top of Union Row from one hour before the start. Timing is by chip, with mats at the start and finish. Results are posted on the Women on the Move website the same day.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN
Event: Women on the Move Community Run 7K
Date: Sunday 11 July 2027
Applicant: Women on the Move Port Halden
Prepared by: Tessera Event Transport
Issue: 1.2

1. Scope
This plan describes how traffic will be managed for the Women on the Move Community Run 7K, a 7K race in the Tanners Row area of Port Halden with a 08:00 start. It has been prepared to accompany the permit application and should be read with the race plan. See the attached correspondence from the police for the escort.

Some background. Our committee has run races in this part of Port Halden for a number of years, and most of our members live locally. The council's traffic controller looked over an early sketch of the route last year, though not this version of the plan.

2. Road closures
The principal closure will be on Union Row. Elsewhere on the course, traffic will be held dynamically by the appointed contractor as the field passes, in line with accepted industry practice. Signal Hill Traffic Services will confirm the detailed arrangements following a pre-event site visit.

3. Major crossings
Busier junctions along the course will receive appropriate supervision during the event. Staffing levels will be determined by Signal Hill Traffic Services on the morning, taking account of conditions at the time, with resources deployed flexibly to where they are most needed.

4. Diversions
Signed diversions will operate for the duration of the closures.
- Union Row: traffic diverted via Prince Street and Ferry Road, signed from Canon Road
- Hatter Street: traffic diverted via Cross Avenue and Station Road, signed from Linden Avenue
- Bridge Row: traffic diverted via Regent Road and High Street, signed from Spring Way
- Ash Avenue: traffic diverted via Dock Road and Ferry Road, signed from Copper Row
- Vine Street: traffic diverted via Station Road and Canal Road, signed from Canon Road

5. Emergency vehicle access
A clear lane of at least 3.5 m will be kept along the closed section for emergency vehicles. Barrier staff hold radios on the event channel and can open any closure within two minutes on request from the event controller, who is in direct contact with the police and ambulance control rooms.

6. Notification
All frontages on the closed streets receive a letter drop 21 days before the event, with a further reminder at 7 days. Advance notice signs go up 10 days before, and bus operators have been given the closure times.

7. Reopening
Roads will be reopened following the conclusion of the event, once barriers and equipment have been removed by the contractor.
